thread:
alex: Heads-up — spotting steady KV cache growth on long-context workloads with paged attention. After ~300 tokens the page table shows a bunch of tombstone entries and eviction rate drops, memory climbs until OOM on H100. repro script attached. :eyes:

maria: Can you paste the minimal repro and the exact model/quantization you used? H100 config or a100? Also which runtime build?

alex: H100, 4x80GB, runtime build: r-2026.03.14 (latest main). Model: open-llama-7B quantized int8. Repro steps: 
```bash
# start server
./run_infer --gpu h100 --model open-llama-7b-q8 --paged-attn --kv-cache-size 48G
# client
python stress_longctx.py --seq 8192 --batch 1 --iterations 5
```
Logs snippet: 
```
[2026-03-14T12:34:02Z] kvcache: page_alloc id=0x7f9 tombstone_count=128 skip_evict=true
[2026-03-14T12:34:03Z] pager: eviction loop stalled, pending_free=0, inuse_pages=32768
[2026-03-14T12:34:04Z] mem: process_rss=61GB, gpu_vram_used=45GB
```

jordan: Interesting. I saw something similar last quarter but that was an async free ordering bug on MI250. Can you collect a kvcache trace with `KV_TRACE=1` (captures page map ops + refcounts)? Also dump `pt_shadow` for the PID.

alex: uploaded KV_TRACE and pt_shadow to the thread (link). Quick grep: `free_page()` gets called but page remains tombstoned in pt_shadow. refcount shows 0 but owner bit still set.

linh: Repro'd locally on an H100 dev node — behavior diverges vs RTX: eviction background worker runs but coalescer doesn't pick those page-ranges because their compacted-key is zeroed (i think we hit a hash-collision stall in slotmap). Patch idea: make tombstone sweep synchronous when free backlog > threshold.

maria: Hmm, synchronous sweep may regress latency. Could we instead mark those page ranges for fast reclaim and force a tiny compaction pass? Also need to check kernel selection path — the tiled kernel assumes contiguous pages; noncontig tombstones cause fallback to slowfill which increases event-loop latency.

alex: Confirmed — when tombstone density > ~0.3% we drop into slowfill kernel and throughput collapses. Attaching profiling flamegraph from perf-bot. :bug:

perf-bot: Profile job 1755556799 completed: cpu time hotspots: pager::coalesce(41%), kvcache::lookup(18%), slowfill_kernel(25%). GPU: slowfill kernel dominates at 62% of kernel time.

jordan: That points to two things: (1) bug in page-table free path leaving stale owner flags; (2) kernel selection heuristic not hedging for fragmented PT. My suggestion: add a PT-consistency check in the free path to clear owner masks and decrement shadow counters, then have kernel selector sample fragmentation metric and prefer tiled kernel only when contiguous run >= threshold.

linh: I pushed a small debug patch that logs `pt_owner_mask` changes and bumped the fragmentation threshold locally — it reduced slowfill occurrences in the repro by 80%. Patch: 
```diff
diff --git a/runtime/pager.cc b/runtime/pager.cc
index 123..abc 100644
@@ -432,6 +432,12 @@ void free_page(PageId p) {
+  // ensure owner flags cleared before tombstone creation
+  if (pt_shadow[p].owner_mask.load()) {
+    pt_shadow[p].owner_mask.store(0);
+    pt_shadow[p].refcount.fetch_sub(1);
+  }
+
   tombstone_create(p);
 }
```

maria: Nice. Can you run the standard regression suite? Need to ensure we don't double-free or undercount. Also file a follow-up to evaluate perf impact on <2% fragmentation cases.

alex: Running regression now on H100 and MI250. Early results: H100 repro suppressed, MI250 still shows a rare path where `atomic compare-and-swap` races and tombstone stays.

jordan: If CAS races persist we might need a stronger backoff or a single-writer epoch for PT metadata updates. That adds complexity but is safer than occasional leaks.

linh: I'll open an RFC for an epoch-based PT mutator and add integration tests that fuzz concurrent free/alloc across NVLINK and PCIe transfers.

alex: TL;DR — probable root: stale owner bit + fragmentation triggers slowfill kernel. Mitigation: clear owner in free path + tweak kernel-selection fragmentation threshold. Follow-ups: epoch-based PT fix (jordan/linh), perf regression sweep (maria), CI job matrix across H100/RTX/MI250 (alex). :thumbsup:
